chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sahl, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Hakam, from Abu Ja'far al-Thani (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who died and left his two maternal aunts and his adherents, he (peace be upon him) said: 'The possessors of relationships are nearer to each other' – the wealth is divided between the two maternal aunts.
ai.seo_question: How is inheritance distributed between two maternal aunts according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the inheritance rights of maternal aunts ('Khaltayn') by applying the Quranic principle of 'Ulul-Arham' (those of kinship), establishing that they inherit in the absence of closer agnatic heirs. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on blood ties ('Arham') as a basis for inheritance distribution, distinguishing it from strict patrilineal lines, and underscores the practical application of Quranic verses in resolving specific familial estate disputes.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Sahl, from Al Husayn Bin Al Hakam, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>

the 2nd regarding a man who died and left his two maternal aunts and his adherents. Heasws said: ‘[8:75] and the possessors of relationships are nearer to each other – the wealth is between the two maternal aunts’.
en.sarwar: 7. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Sahf ibn Ziyad from af-Husayn ibn af-Hakam who has narrated the folfowing: “About the case of a man who dies leaving behind his two maternal aunts and relatives, abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘Relatives have priorities over each other. The legacy belongs to the two maternal aunts.”’
